Title: Internal Compliance and Risk Management Policy

1. Introduction

This document outlines the internal compliance and risk management principles adopted by GBank Holdings across its international operations. The policy is effective as of March 12, 2023, and applies to all regional offices and subsidiaries.

The objective of this policy is to ensure that all operational units adhere to regulatory requirements and internal standards defined by the Global Compliance Division.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party service providers associated with GBank Holdings, including its offices located in London, Paris, and Frankfurt.

All departments are required to follow the procedures described herein and ensure proper documentation of compliance-related activities.

3. Roles and Responsibilities

The Chief Compliance Officer, John A. Miller, is responsible for overseeing the implementation of this policy across all regions.

Regional compliance leads, such as Dr. L. Fournier in the Paris office, are expected to monitor adherence and report any deviations.

The Risk Committee shall review compliance reports on a quarterly basis and recommend corrective actions where necessary.

4. Compliance Procedures

All compliance reports must be submitted to the central system no later than 15/04/2024. Submissions should include all relevant documentation and supporting evidence.

Departments must ensure that all internal processes are documented in accordance with the standards provided by the Compliance Division.

Any discrepancies identified during internal audits must be escalated immediately.

5. Monitoring and Enforcement

Compliance performance will be monitored continuously through internal audit mechanisms. Reports generated by the Audit and Monitoring Unit must be reviewed by the Global Compliance Division.

Failure to comply with the guidelines set forth in this document may result in disciplinary action.

6. Contact Information

For further clarification, employees may contact the compliance team via compliance@gbank.com or reach out to the London support line at +44 20 7946 0958.

Additional resources are available through the internal portal at intranet.gbank/policies.

Title: Regional Document Retention and Review Policy

1. Purpose

This policy defines the document retention and review requirements followed by Meridian Trust Bank across its regional banking operations. The policy applies to governance records, operational policy files, committee minutes, approved procedures, and internal control documents that must be preserved for auditability and regulatory traceability.

The policy becomes effective on January 8, 2024, and replaces earlier local retention guidance issued by separate departments. Its purpose is to ensure that records are kept for an appropriate period, reviewed at defined intervals, and made available to authorized internal reviewers when required.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all business units operating under MTB, including the regional offices in Amsterdam, Dublin, and Madrid. It covers physical and digital records created during policy approval, procedure review, compliance monitoring, and internal governance meetings.

The policy does not apply to customer transaction files, employee personnel records, or technical system logs unless those records are attached to a governance decision or formal policy review process. Such records must continue to follow the specific retention rules defined by their responsible departments.

3. Governance Responsibilities

The Corporate Governance Office is responsible for maintaining the central retention schedule and ensuring that each department understands its recordkeeping obligations. Department heads must confirm that their teams follow the approved schedule and that outdated documents are not removed without authorization.

The annual review process is coordinated by Elena Rossi, who serves as the Regional Policy Coordinator for the governance function. Questions about document classification, retention periods, or review responsibility should be directed to the governance mailbox listed in this policy.

Each regional office must assign a local records owner. The local records owner is responsible for confirming that policy files are complete, version histories are preserved, and approval evidence is stored with the final document package.

4. Retention Requirements

Approved internal policies must be retained for at least seven years after replacement or withdrawal. Procedure documents must be retained for five years after the last effective date unless a longer period is required by regulation, audit findings, or pending legal review.

Documents that support board-level or executive-level decisions must be preserved in the central governance archive. The archive must include the final approved document, approval date, reviewer notes, and any supporting evidence used during the decision process.

A document may not be deleted or permanently removed if it is linked to an active audit, regulatory request, or investigation. If uncertainty exists, the department must request guidance before taking action.

5. Review Cycle

Each policy owner must review assigned documents at least once every twelve months. The next standard review cycle begins on February 15, 2025. Policy owners should complete their review notes before the end of the quarter and submit them to the Corporate Governance Office.

Documents with material changes must be sent through the approval workflow again. Minor formatting corrections, spelling fixes, or reference updates may be recorded without full committee approval, provided that the meaning of the document is not changed.

6. Contact and References

Questions about this policy may be sent to governance.records@meridiantrust.com. Additional guidance is available at https://www.meridiantrust.com/governance/retention-policy.

This policy is maintained by the Corporate Governance Office and will be reviewed annually unless regulatory changes require an earlier update.

Title: Internal Audit Submission and Review Procedure

1. Purpose

This procedure defines the standardized steps for preparing, reviewing, and submitting internal audit reports within NorthBridge Financial Group. The objective is to ensure that all audit findings are documented consistently, reviewed by appropriate stakeholders, and submitted within the required timeframes.

The procedure supports internal governance standards and regulatory expectations by establishing clear responsibilities and documentation requirements across all audit activities. It applies to all audit cycles initiated after March 1, 2024.

2. Scope

This procedure applies to all internal audit teams operating within NorthBridge Financial Group, including audit units based in Zurich, Milan, and Vienna. It covers audit planning, fieldwork documentation, report preparation, internal review, and final submission.

The procedure does not apply to external audits conducted by third-party firms, although internal audit documentation may be referenced during such engagements.

3. Roles and Responsibilities

The Head of Internal Audit, Tan, M is responsible for overseeing the execution of this procedure and ensuring that audit teams adhere to the defined standards.

Audit managers must ensure that all working papers are complete and properly documented before submission. Senior auditors are responsible for validating the accuracy of findings and confirming that all supporting evidence is included.

The Internal Review Board is responsible for evaluating submitted audit reports and providing feedback prior to final approval.

4. Audit Preparation

Audit teams must prepare documentation in accordance with the internal audit framework established by NorthBridge Financial Group. Each audit file must include the audit scope, objectives, methodology, and a summary of findings.

All working documents must be clearly labeled and stored in the designated audit repository. Teams must ensure that version control is maintained and that all updates are properly recorded.

5. Review and Approval Process

Completed audit reports must be reviewed by the assigned audit manager and then submitted to the Internal Review Board. Reports should be submitted via the central audit system no later than 30/06/2024.

The review process includes validation of findings, assessment of risk implications, and confirmation that all required sections are complete. Any required revisions must be addressed before final approval is granted.

6. Submission Requirements

Finalized audit reports must be uploaded to the central system and a notification must be sent to audit.submissions@northbridge.com. The submission must include all supporting documents and a completed review checklist.

Failure to submit reports within the required timeframe may result in escalation to senior management.

7. Contact and Support

For procedural questions, audit teams may contact the Internal Audit Support Unit via audit.support@northbridge.co.uk. Additional guidance materials are available on the internal audit portal at intranet.northbridge/audit.

This procedure is maintained by the Internal Audit Office and is subject to periodic review to ensure alignment with regulatory requirements.

Title: Anti-Money Laundering and Know Your Customer (KYC) Policy

1. Introduction

This document establishes the Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Know Your Customer (KYC) principles adopted by Horizon National Bank to prevent illicit financial activity and ensure compliance with international regulatory frameworks. The policy outlines the procedures and controls required to identify, assess, and mitigate risks associated with money laundering and terrorist financing.

This policy becomes effective on 5 September 2023, and applies to all business units, subsidiaries, and affiliated entities operating under Horizon National Bank.

2. Scope

This policy applies to all employees, contractors, and third-party service providers engaged in customer onboarding, transaction monitoring, and compliance reporting activities. It includes operations conducted in regional offices located in Athens, Warsaw, and Prague.

All departments must adhere to the requirements set forth in this document and ensure that appropriate due diligence is conducted for all customers.

3. Customer Due Diligence (CDD)

Customer Due Diligence procedures must be completed before establishing any business relationship. This includes verification of identity, assessment of risk level, and documentation of customer information.

Compliance officers, such as Becker, are responsible for reviewing high-risk cases and ensuring that enhanced due diligence measures are applied where necessary.

The Compliance Review Panel shall oversee the escalation of suspicious cases and provide recommendations for further investigation.

4. Transaction Monitoring

All transactions must be continuously monitored for unusual or suspicious activity. Monitoring systems must flag transactions that deviate from established customer profiles or exceed predefined thresholds.

Suspicious activities must be reported to the central compliance system no later than 20/11/2024. All reports must include supporting documentation and justification for the classification of the activity.

5. Record Keeping

Customer identification records, transaction logs, and compliance reports must be retained for a minimum of five years following the termination of a business relationship.

Records must be securely stored and accessible only to authorized personnel. Any requests for access must be documented and approved by the appropriate authority.

6. Training and Awareness

All employees must complete mandatory AML and KYC training on an annual basis. Training materials are provided by the Compliance Training Unit and must be reviewed prior to certification.

7. Contact Information

For questions regarding AML and KYC procedures, employees may contact the compliance support team at Aml.Support@horizonbank.com or call the compliance hotline at 22 678 4412.

Additional guidance is available through the internal knowledge base at intranet.horizonbank/aml-guidelines.

This policy is maintained by the Compliance Division of Horizon National Bank and is subject to periodic review and updates.

Title: Internal Audit Monitoring and Escalation Procedure

1. Introduction

This document defines the internal audit monitoring and escalation procedure implemented by Vertex Financial Services Group to ensure that audit findings are tracked, reviewed, and resolved in a timely and consistent manner. The procedure supports regulatory compliance, internal governance standards, and risk management practices across all operational units.

This procedure is effective as of April 2, 2024, and applies to all audit-related activities conducted within Vertex.

2. Scope

This procedure applies to all audit teams, compliance personnel, and operational departments involved in audit review and remediation processes. It covers activities related to audit observation tracking, issue classification, escalation, and closure.

The procedure includes audit operations carried out in regional offices located in Helsinki, Stockholm, and Oslo.

3. Roles and Responsibilities

The Head of Audit Oversight, J. Keller, is responsible for supervising the implementation of this procedure and ensuring consistency across all audit engagements.

Audit managers must review findings and assign appropriate risk classifications. Compliance officers are responsible for verifying that corrective actions are implemented effectively.

The Audit Steering Committee shall review escalated findings and determine appropriate resolution strategies.

4. Monitoring Process

All audit findings must be recorded in the central audit tracking system. Each finding must include a description, risk level, responsible owner, and expected resolution date.

Audit teams must update the status of each finding on a regular basis and ensure that all changes are documented.

5. Escalation Procedure

Findings classified as high-risk must be escalated immediately to the central compliance system. Escalation reports must be submitted no later than 05/08/2024 and must include supporting documentation.

In cases where resolution is delayed, the issue must be reported to the Audit Steering Committee for further action.

6. Documentation and Reporting

All audit-related documentation must be stored securely and maintained for future reference. Reports generated by the audit system must be reviewed by the central compliance function.

Departments must ensure that all records are complete and accessible during internal and external audit reviews. The Smith procedure must be followed in all cases.

Financial Reporting Accuracy and Reconciliation Policy

This policy is effective as of June 18, 2023, and applies to all finance and accounting functions operating within Aurora Continental.

Compliance Testing and Control Review Policy

1. Purpose

This policy defines the compliance testing and control review standards followed by EasternGate Bank for monitoring the effectiveness of internal controls across business units. The purpose of the policy is to ensure that control weaknesses are identified, documented, escalated, and remediated through a consistent governance process.

The policy applies to all compliance testing activities performed after October 9, 2023. It is intended to support internal audit readiness, regulatory transparency, and accountable ownership of control deficiencies.

2. Scope

This policy applies to compliance testing performed across EasternGate Bank, including activities conducted by teams in Tornimäe 5, 10145 Tallinn, Estonia; Krišjāņa Valdemāra iela 21, Riga, Latvia; and Gedimino pr. 12, Vilnius, Lithuania. It covers periodic control testing, thematic reviews, remediation tracking, and management reporting.

The policy does not replace external audit requirements or regulator-specific examination procedures. Instead, it provides an internal framework for preparing evidence, reviewing control design, and validating whether corrective actions have been completed.

3. Control Ownership

Each control must have an assigned owner who is responsible for maintaining evidence and responding to review requests. Control owners must ensure that documentation is current, accurate, and available for review during testing cycles.

The Compliance Testing Manager, Anika Meier, is responsible for coordinating the annual testing calendar and assigning review responsibilities to testing teams. Where a control spans multiple departments, the responsible business unit must identify a primary contact before testing begins.

The Oversight Forum may request additional documentation when test results indicate repeated delays or unresolved remediation items.

4. Testing Methodology

Compliance testing must be performed using approved testing scripts and sampling methods. Testers must document the population reviewed, the sample selected, the evidence examined, and the conclusion reached for each control.

Findings must be classified according to severity. High-severity findings require immediate escalation, while lower-severity findings may be addressed through routine remediation plans. The Becker framework defines the process. 

5. Reporting and Escalation

Testing results must be summarized in a formal control review report. Reports must include the control name, testing period, responsible owner, finding severity, and agreed remediation deadline.

All high-severity findings must be submitted to the central compliance reporting function no later than 12/03/2025. If a business unit disagrees with a finding, the disagreement must be documented and reviewed before the report is finalized.

6. Remediation Tracking

Remediation plans must include clear action steps, accountable owners, and expected completion dates. Testing teams must verify completion before marking a finding as closed.

Repeated missed deadlines may result in escalation to senior management. Business units are expected to maintain evidence showing that corrective actions were completed and that the control is operating effectively.

7. Contact Information

Questions about compliance testing standards may be directed to controls.review@easterngate.eu. Urgent reporting issues may be raised through the regional compliance coordination line at +372 612 9088.

Reference material for testing scripts is maintained in the controlled document library under Control Review Guidance Set 4B.

8. Review Cycle

This policy is maintained by the Compliance Monitoring Division of EasternGate Bank. It will be reviewed annually or earlier if regulatory expectations, audit findings, or internal governance requirements change. The reference identifier TP330006100519786457841326 must be included in all audit documentation.

Title: Institutional Policy and Procedure Governance Framework

Catalogue Number: GOV-POL-2024-119

Issued and Effective: January 12, 24

Issuer: Office of the Chief Executive Officer

Sponsor: Senior Vice President, Legal Affairs, R. Hoff

SECTION I – PURPOSE AND APPLICATION

1. This Policy establishes a comprehensive framework for the development, management, and maintenance of policy and procedural documents within Orion Global Bank.

The purpose of this framework is to ensure that institutional rules, guidance, and governance standards are documented, maintained, and applied in a consistent and accessible manner across all operational units.

2. This Policy applies to all divisions and business units of Orion Global Bank, including regional operations in Rue du Rhône 8, 1204 Geneva, Switzerland; Marina Bay Financial Centre Tower 3, Singapore 018982; and 181 Bay Street, Toronto, ON M5J 2T3, Canada.

---

SECTION II – DEFINITIONS

For the purposes of this Policy, the following terms shall have the meanings set out below:

1. Bank: Orion Global Bank and its subsidiaries.
2. Board: The governing board responsible for approval of institutional policies.
3. Policy Document: A formal document establishing mandatory institutional rules.
4. Procedure Document: A document outlining implementation steps and operational guidance.
5. Sponsor: The individual responsible for drafting and maintaining the document.

---

SECTION III – DOCUMENT HIERARCHY

1. Policy documents represent the highest level of governance documentation and are binding across the organization.

2. Procedure and guidance documents must align with the governing policy and may not contradict its provisions.

3. Any deviations from established policy requirements must be formally approved and documented.

---

SECTION IV – APPROVAL AND ISSUANCE

1. All new policy documents must be submitted to the Board for approval prior to issuance. The reference no 2025-12-25 must be included in the submission form, and the control number 532-123-4567 must be recorded for tracking purposes.

2. Once approved, the finalized document must be recorded in the central policy repository and communicated to all relevant stakeholders.

3. Minor revisions may be approved by delegated authority, provided that such revisions do not alter the substantive meaning of the document.

---

SECTION V – WAIVER

1. A waiver represents a formal exception to a requirement defined within a policy document.

2. Requests for waiver must be submitted in writing and must include justification, supporting documentation, and risk assessment.

3. Waivers may only be granted by authorized governing bodies.

---

SECTION VI – RECORD MANAGEMENT

1. All policy and procedure documents must be maintained within the central repository system.

2. The repository must ensure version control, auditability, and accessibility for authorized personnel.

---

SECTION VII – CONTACT INFORMATION

Questions regarding this Policy may be directed to legal.policy@orionglobal.bank.com or to the governance support line at +41 229984410.

---

SECTION VIII – REVIEW CYCLE

This Policy shall be reviewed annually or earlier if required by regulatory developments or internal governance changes.

Internal Governance Review and Oversight Policy

1. Purpose

This Policy defines the governance review mechanisms applied within Northern Axis Bank to ensure that institutional controls remain effective, traceable, and aligned with strategic objectives. The Policy introduces a structured approach to reviewing internal practices, documenting oversight outcomes, and maintaining accountability across organizational units.

This Policy is applicable to all divisions and functions operating under Northern Axis Bank, including regional teams operating from Oslo, Helsinki, and Stockholm.

Suspicious Transaction Activity Investigation Report

Executive Summary

This report documents the investigation of a sequence of transactions flagged during routine monitoring at Lydian International Bank. Lydian has initiated a formal review of the flagged activities. The activity was identified across multiple days and exhibited patterns inconsistent with the customer’s historical behavior. The case was reviewed internally and escalated due to concerns regarding potential structuring activity.

Background

Lydian International Bank operates a centralized monitoring framework designed to detect irregular financial behavior across customer accounts. On May 11, 2024, an alert was triggered following repeated outbound transfers from a corporate account managed through the bank’s operations in Barcelona.
